chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Quitting school for the Marigold Ballroom; his mother's visit
summary: Fed up in the speakeasy, Norvo calls Jack Tebo, who gets him a job directing the Marigold band in Minneapolis; his mother comes to visit just as he is leaving.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Was in that band, and they'd come inbetween shows, maybe -- so I was there -- Wefland said, 'Wait, you said "No." come back, you don't want to (unintelligible), so I went out and had something to eat and I came back was going to meet him. And, so I was in that speakeasy and I was thinking, what am I doing. I'd packed up -- I hadn't played for a couple of months or more. I said this is silly. This is really not what I want to do. I am not interested in school whatsoever. I feel more at home with people like Wefland and the people around me so I called Tiboo, and I said, I can't take it any longer. He said 'Well, my gosh you just -- Ish just took the band, he's happy.' I said, 'No, no, no. I don't mean that. Just get me a job someplace.' So he called -- he said, 'Stayed -- stay right there. Stay right there. I'll see what I can do. I'll call you back today.'
He thought the world of you, didn't he?
Cause he discovered you from the beginning.

Yeah. And he was a -- he called me back. And said, 'I got you a job directing the band at the Marigold Ballroom at Minneapolis.' I said, 'I'll take it.' And I took it. My mother came into town, she was coming in -- with laurels

of good tidings, I was -- finally pleasing her. She arrives at 8:00 o'clock. I met her and I said, 'I'm going -- I'm quitting school I'm going to Minneapolis.' She said, 'I'm glad to see you made a decision.' I turned around, put her on a train at 10:00 o'clock, I took the mid -- the noon train the next day. Got my things packed. Shipped everything to Minneapolis and I opened in about -- that weekend.
Well you mean to say your mother came in to see how you were doing and everything and you put her on the train two hours later?
She came to see me, you know, visit me. And, with the idea she said, 'Well, I know that --'
I to -- know that's probably right for you, you've to -- got to do what you want to do.
And she said, 'I'll go back home and I said well, I'm going to Minneapolis, you come and -- will you come and visit me?' She said, 'Yeah.'
Well she was great, wasn't she?
Yeah. So I worked there for awhile --
The only one to take offense was Glenn,
